Remarks: 
Description: We will be kicking off the new schoolyear preparing for the Biking + Camping trip at Hickory Run State Park! To prepare for the trip\, our first two meetings will be cycling themed.  We'll focus on Bike Maintenance & Repair\, Laws & Safety and Riding techniques. 

If you have a Bike (pedal only\, no electrics…)\, please bring it to the next two meetings\, along with your helmet.   

We will have tools and instructions to help teach you to tune up your own bike\, practice fixing flats and other requirements for Cycling Merit Badge. We will also be doing normal camping preparations and meal planning for the camping trip. Note\, that this trip can then count toward one of the required rides for Cycling or one of the camping experiences needed for Camping Merit Badge.  

In preparation\, please read through the Cycling Merit Badge Book:  https://filestore.scouting.org/filestore/Merit_Badge_ReqandRes/Pamphlets/Cycling_2025.pdf

___________________________

Now that school has started\, we're moving back to our regular weekly meeting schedule and Class A shirts are expected for all Scouts attending!

Going forward\, we'll be holding parent meetings as part of most Scout meetings to help the Troop run more efficiently and effectively.  Looking forward to seeing everyone!

Remarks: 
Description: Hello Troop 99!
We'll be taking advantage of the beautiful early fall weather in September and heading north to Hickory Run and Lehigh Gorge State Parks for a weekend of camping\, cycling\, hiking and overall fun outdoors! This trip will be much more relaxed than last year\, owing to the fact that there will be no train schedules\, early morning commutes\, or urban parking scrambles involved.

We plan for a 15 mile bike trip along with camping\, cooking and maybe a hike through amazing glacial formation that is Boulder Field. This is a BYOB trip (Bring Your Own Bike)\, we won't be using an outfitter this year. Important Note: Helmets are REQUIRED for this trip. We will be emphasizing safety throughout the day\, including the buddy system and taking water breaks regularly.

If you have any immediate questions\, please feel free to reach out to me.
Let's get ready for an awesome biking adventure!
Yours in Scouting\,

Mr. Schrecengost

Remarks: Assemble Wooden Cubbies for CRN Wrestling Team
Description: My Eagle Service Project consists of assembling wooden cubicles for the CR North Wrestling team to store their gear throughout the season. This is a need that the wrestling coaches have mentioned multiple times throughout last season.  I arranged for volunteers this summer to clean out the room and paint it in preparation for these cubicle units to be installed.  

Volunteers will help assemble precut wooden pieces to create the units. They will need to have holes puttied\, be sanded\, primed\, and painted. After this is completed they will be installed permanently to the wrestling room wall.   This project will help keep the wrestling team organized and give them a sense of purpose and pride in their sport. 

NOTE:  The initial work will be completed off-site at a carpentry workshop in Florence\, NJ.

Description: Hello Troop 99!
Get ready for our annual Winter Games Campout\, December 12th-14th! This year\, we'll be heading to the beautiful Hidden Valley Scout Reservation in Loysville\, PA where we have booked the Labor Lodge\, an awesome 50 person cabin with indoor restrooms\, a giant kitchen\, plenty of tables and extra-thick mattresses!  The adult leaders provide all of the food and beverages for the weekend\, the Scouts need to bring their favorite board/card/role playing games and a willingness to have fun!

This is an excellent opportunity for parents and scouts who haven't been on many camping trips to get involved and build some memories with their fellow troop members.  Parents are highly encouraged to attend\, but they must be registered with the Troop and Council to participate.

Remarks: Camping and hiking at Valley Forge
Description: We will be exploring Valley Forge National Historic Park\,  where General George Washington and the Continental Army spent the winter of 1777-1778 and regarded by many as the birthplace of the American Army. 

On Friday night we will set up camp at the Valley Forge Scout Campground\, located a half mile from the Park\, a wooded campsite with an important amenity - heated bathrooms.

On Saturday we will go to the park with a stop in the Visitor's Center to learn about Valley Forge and then hike the Valley Forge Historical Trail to see the encampment\, artillery park\, Washington's Headquarters and other sites. We will head back to camp for the night and return to the Legion on Sunday morning.

This trip is a great opportunity to complete cooking requirements\, including a trail meal.

Remarks: Camping and Rafting in the Lehigh Gorge!
Description: Get ready for a thrill! T99 will be braving the Lehigh River at the Whitewater Challengers Raft-O-Ree!  This is a special Scout weekend that includes a dam release. That means that water levels are guaranteed to be high enough to have an awesome time on the river!  We'll be camping Friday night and hitting the river Saturday morning at 10:05!  
• Two nights of Camping - Friday and Saturday nights.
• Whitewater Rafting on Saturday. Rafting check-in time is the time listed above for your "Raft-O-Ree."
• River lunch on Saturday. Be sure to pick up your lunches before being fitted for life jackets.
• Scout Patch and Certificate of Achievement.
Important Information About Camping
• AMENITIES: We welcome you to make use our complimentary sand volleyball courts\, basketball court\, recreation field\, hot showers & restrooms\, free Wi-Fi\, and cell phone charging stations.
• ALSO ON SITE: Snack bar\, camp store and a private pavilion available to rent.
Important Information About Rafting
• TRIP LENGTH: Trip lengths vary from day to day based on weather and water conditions\, but we estimate your trip will be approximately 2.5 to 3 hours on the river\, 5 to 6 hours of your day overall.

Remarks: Canoeing on Neshaminy Creek
Description: Hello Troop 99!
We have adjusted the plan for this weekend\, we are going canoeing on Neshaminy Creek instead of the Delaware.  This will be a day trip\, putting in at Bridge point Park in Doylestown and pulling out at the Boathouse in Tyler Park\, 14.5 miles of paddling. 

WHEN: Saturday\,  August 29th
MEETING POINT: American Legion Hall — 9:00 AM sharp
ROUTE: Bridge Point Park (Doylestown) → Tyler State Park (Newtown)
DISTANCE: 14.5 miles
ESTIMATED TIME ON WATER: 4–5 hours
EXPECTED RETURN: ~3:30–4:30 PM


WHAT TO EXPECT:
- A full-day paddle on Neshaminy Creek — mostly flatwater with some ripples and Class I rapids
- Pass under the historic Schofield Ford Covered Bridge
- Scenic creek through Bucks County farmland and woodlands
- Paddle is gentle — about 3 mph

WHAT SCOUTS SHOULD BRING:
✅ Water bottles — at least 1 liter per person!
✅ Lunch and snacks
✅ Sunscreen — bring extra\, water reflects sun all day
✅ Bug Repellent
✅ Water shoes or old sneakers — shoes that can get wet and have good grip (NO flip-flops)
✅ Quick-dry clothing — NO cotton! 
✅ Hat with brim 
✅ Sunglasses (with strap)
✅ Change of dry clothes — including socks and underwear\, in a plastic bag
✅ Toilet paper — wrap it in a ziplock bag 
✅ Small towel
✅ Small dry bag or ziplock bags for phone/keys

PARENT VOLUNTEERS NEEDED:
We need drivers to help shuttle the canoes and Scouts!
Depending on the number of Scouts on the trip\, we need few drivers willing to ride along with the crew up to Doylestown and then drop vehicles off at Tyler Park by the boathouse (including the truck & trailer).
Our goal is to be able to pull out at Tyler and not have to shuttle back and forth to Doylestown afterward. 

- Arrive at American Legion Hall at 9:00 AM to load paddles and PFD's with trailer
- Drive the trailer to Bridge Point Park (put-in) and unload
- Drive the empty trailer directly to Tyler State Park (take-out)
- Meet the group at Tyler State Park or Legion Hall\, depending on # of Scouts upon return.

If you can help as a driver with a truck and trailer\, please let me know.


WEATHER PLAN:
Water levels on Neshaminy Creek are monitored (USGS gauge near Rushland). If conditions aren't safe\, we'll postpone. Scouts/parents will be notified by 7:00 AM on trip morning if the trip is cancelled.

Scouts and Adults who did not attend or staff at summer.  Non Swimmers or Beginners may be allowed on the trip\,  but will be required to canoe with an Adult Swimmer. Non-swimmers and beginners on the trip may be limited in the areas they can swim in on the river.  If you want to go and have not taken a Swim test\, please reach out to me.  There are a limited number of Adult Swimmers on the trip\, so seats are not guaranteed for non-swimmers.

We have a limited number of canoes\, so sign up now!

YiS\,

Mr. Schrecengost
